t.7.46.1: Then the younger brother of Rāghava, having first placed Maithilī aboard, himself boarded the very spacious, well-equipped boat of the Niṣādas.
t.7.46.2: Tormented by grief, Lakṣmaṇa told Sumantra, who was with the chariot, "Wait here," and told the boatman, "Set forth."
t.7.46.3: Then, having reached the bank of the Bhāgīrathī, Lakṣmaṇa, with joined palms and his voice choked with tears, spoke these words to Maithilī.
t.7.46.4: A great dart is lodged in my heart, O Vaidehī, because in this matter I have been made by the wise noble one an object of the world's reproach.
t.7.46.5: Better for me indeed is death today, or whatever might be worse than death, and I should not be appointed to such a deed as this, condemned by the world.
t.7.46.6: "Be gracious, O lady of noble vows, and you should not be angry with me." Saying this, Lakṣmaṇa, his palms joined in reverence, fell to the ground.
t.7.46.7: Seeing Lakṣmaṇa weeping with joined palms and longing for his own death, Maithilī, deeply agitated, spoke these words to him.
t.7.46.8: What is this? I do not understand; tell me truly, Lakṣmaṇa. I see that you are not at ease. Is all well with the king?
t.7.46.9: You are adjured by the lord of men: whatever anguish you hold within yourself, tell it to me here in my presence. I command you.
t.7.46.10: But Lakṣmaṇa, being urged by Vaidehī, his mind dejected, his face cast down and his throat choked with tears, spoke these words.
t.7.46.11: O daughter of Janaka, having heard in the midst of the assembly a most dreadful slander concerning you, spread both in the city and throughout the countryside,
t.7.46.12: O Devī, those matters which the king has laid away in his heart are not to be spoken by me in your presence; his resentment has been put behind him.
t.7.46.13: You, though blameless, have been abandoned by the king in my presence, for he fears the censure of the citizens; O queen, you must not take it otherwise.
t.7.46.15: This, here on the bank of the Jāhnavī, is the ascetic grove of the brahmarṣis, holy and delightful; do not give way to despair, O auspicious one.
t.7.46.14: Having heeded the king's command, I must leave you on the outskirts of the hermitages; such, it is said, is your craving.
t.7.46.16: This bull among sages, the Brahmin Vālmīki of very great fame, was the closest friend of my father, King Daśaratha.
t.7.46.17: Taking refuge in the shade of the feet of this great-souled one, dwell here in happiness, O daughter of Janaka, intent on fasting and with a single-pointed mind.
t.7.46.18: Taking up the vow of a devoted wife and keeping Rāma always in your heart, O queen, by acting thus the highest good will be yours.
